authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: In development and validation evidence, the plain DDoS-to-Benign rate exceeded the paired clean rate; the defended rate was lower than the plain rate. Reconstruction attribution distance decreased toward a paired preattack clean reference, not an oracle clean state.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.605109, versus 0.077628 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.121974, an absolute reduction of 0.483134 from the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000; maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.100000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.687736 to 0.283871, with recovery fraction 0.587239.

interpretations.statement: Observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class; it does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refuse to assert malicious intent: it is unsupported by the evidence.
Refuse to claim oracle clean recovery: oracle-clean attribution state was unavailable.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator is a paired round 4 preattack reference, not an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable and not substituted.
Per-client detector scores and numeric thresholds were not materialized.
Evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
